evidence.note: Built self-authored CPU diagnostics comparing JAX vs torch embed_prefix and embed_suffix outputs with explicit tolerances (prefix max ~3e-4 = match, suffix max ~0.915 = fail), then narrowed to state token vs action tokens vs time embedding — genuine layer/method-level parity checks.

Deeper intermediate diagnostic comparing action_in_proj, time concat, both MLPs, and swish stages against JAX (~1e-5), localizing an extra second-swish bug — component-level numerical verification driving the fix.

After benchmark showed sampling parity gap (~7.38e-4 vs 5e-4 gate), addressed determinism/precision by forcing float32, disabling TF32, and matching JAX mask constant, then re-verified — determinism awareness under fixed inputs.

Re-ran benchmark.py (which checks loss+sampling parity PASS/FAIL, not just latency) after each optimization (KV-cache, torch.compile, revert), confirming output equivalence rather than trusting latency alone.
Used traceback and parameter-key comparison scripts to catch shape/topology mismatches (scan-axis squeeze, missing ViT attention biases) before trusting the load.

reasoning: The agent built layer-level/per-method numerical comparisons against the JAX reference (embed_prefix, embed_suffix, action tokens, time embedding, intermediate MLP/swish stages) with explicit tolerances, localized divergence precisely, addressed determinism via precision/TF32 controls, and re-ran benchmark.py's parity+latency check after every optimization rather than trusting the latency number — matching the level-8 anchor. It falls short of 10 because these diagnostics were built reactively to debug failures rather than as a pre-designed systematic harness, and post-optimization parity leaned on benchmark.py rather than independent per-method re-checks against frozen model.py, with no explicit guard against the PASS status being gamed.
